- New `.github/workflows/minds-evals-scheduled.yml`: a nightly (11:00 UTC) Minds persona eval run against two mngr and default-workspace-template pairs, both repos at `main` and both at the `minds-v<version>` tag the stable release channel names. Each pair is frozen to SHAs up front, gated behind a cheap oracle pass, and skipped when a green marker already covers that exact (mngr SHA, dwt SHA, config). The eval harness and the live staging tier are not part of that key, so the `released` pair -- whose refs are the release tag -- is verified once per release unless a run is dispatched with `force`; the README says so. It runs in its own concurrency groups and nothing in the release procedure waits on it.

- The pairs are independent of each other end to end: a pair whose refs do not resolve -- a `minds-v<version>` tag not yet pushed to both repos -- is reported as unresolved and left out of the run rather than costing the other pair its answer. Dependencies install from `apps/minds_evals/uv.lock` or the run fails, so the only thing that moves between two nights is the pair of SHAs.

- The workflow can be dispatched by hand with `pair` (`main` / `released` / `both`), a one-off `mngr_ref` / `dwt_ref` pair, a different `config` (empty uses the small config, which is also what a schedule gets), `force` to bypass the green-marker skip, and `skip_live` to run only the oracle pass. A ref or config that is not shaped like one is refused up front.

- Results land as two per-pair artifacts kept for 14 days: the check-run summaries, and the full job directories minus the workspace snapshots. Every Modal environment a run creates carries a `ci-<timestamp>-` scope in its name and is deleted by name at the end of the job, with an 8-hour age-based sweep over that scope as the backstop. Developer environments are out of reach of both.

- A Slack notification job reports each pair's refs, SHAs, verdict, and per-case rows, naming the pass that actually broke and whether its summary was missing or unreadable. Its verdict covers the eval job as a whole, so a run whose every pair passed but whose job went red or was cancelled -- a cleanup that could not delete the run's Modal environments, say -- is flagged rather than reported as a clean success; a run that went red because a pair failed is reported as that, without pointing at cleanup. It reads its webhook from `mngr/ci/SLACK_MINDS_EVALS_WEBHOOK`; until that secret exists it warns and writes the same report to the run summary rather than failing, and a notification that cannot look up the run's duration still reports everything else.

- The per-trial table is published whichever way a pass went, including when the pass itself broke rather than merely graded red -- which is the run whose rows are most worth reading. A dispatch input that is not shaped like a ref, or names a config that does not exist on the branch, is refused in the free resolve job before any paid runner starts.

- The `test-minds-evals` CI gate also runs when the scheduled workflow itself changes. That suite reads the workflow's `CI_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` and pins it to the environment name a CI trial creates, so editing the workflow alone used to leave that pin unchecked -- and a prefix that matches nothing leaks the run's live Modal environments in silence.

- New `just minds-evals-list-environments` prints the Modal environments a developer's own eval run left behind without touching any of them, and `just minds-evals-cleanup-environments` deletes exactly those. Both are opt-in and scoped to that run's job directory.

- A push to a branch named `minds-evals-run/<anything>` runs the workflow for the main pair without a dispatch, which GitHub accepts only once the file is on the default branch: the oracle pass only, or the live pass too when the head commit message carries `[live]`. This is how a change to the workflow is exercised before it merges.
